name: StudyKit
tagline: Turns your course material into flashcards, quizzes and study notes, then drills you on them.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core loop here is genuinely simple: chunk a PDF, ask a model for question and answer pairs, store them, schedule reviews with a spaced repetition algorithm. An agent can build that for one person in a single sitting, and the flashcard quality will be roughly as good as the paid version because both are just prompting the same class of model. The gaps are everything around it: a mobile app you actually reach for on the bus, offline decks, handwriting and slide OCR, lecture audio and video ingestion, and sync between your laptop and phone. If you study at a desk, the DIY build is fine. If you study in the gaps of your day, you are rebuilding a mobile app, and that is not one session.
coreLoopDIY: Upload a PDF or paste text, get generated flashcards and multiple choice questions into a local SQLite deck, then drill them with an SM-2 spaced repetition queue.
requirements: An LLM API key (OpenAI or Anthropic), billed per use
Your source material as PDF or plain text, since handwriting and video need extra work
whatYouLose: Mobile apps with offline decks, which is where most actual studying happens
Ingestion of lecture recordings, slides and handwritten notes without you doing the conversion
Cross-device sync and backups you do not have to think about
Prompt tuning someone else already did, so your first generated cards will be more repetitive and more trivia-shaped
Shared or community decks and anything social that keeps you coming back
moatNotes: Study tools live or die on friction. The algorithm is public domain, the polish and the phone in your pocket are the product.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because studying is a discipline problem, not a software problem, and paying for a tool that already works on your phone removes one excuse. The generation step is commodity, but the thing that gets used is the one that opens in two seconds on a bus, remembers where you were, and does not require you to convert a lecture recording by hand first. Students also tend to pay in short bursts around exams, where a monthly fee is cheaper than a weekend of building.
notes: The spaced repetition math is fifty years old and free; you are paying for it to be pleasant.
prompt:
Build a local-first personal study app called deckbench. Single user, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Vite + React + TypeScript for the UI
- Express (TypeScript) API on port 8787
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/deckbench.db, migrations run on boot
- pdf-parse for PDF text extraction
- OpenAI Node SDK, model and key from .env (OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_MODEL), never hardcoded
- Tailwind for styling, no component library

Features in scope:
1. Decks: create, rename, delete. A deck holds cards and sources.
2. Ingest: upload a PDF or paste raw text. Extract text, split into ~1500 character chunks on paragraph boundaries, store chunks with their source.
3. Generate: for each chunk, one LLM call that returns strict JSON: an array of items with front, back, type ("basic" or "mcq"), and for mcq an options array plus correct index. Validate with zod, drop malformed items, do not crash. Show a review screen where I accept, edit or reject each generated card before it enters the deck.
4. Study: SM-2 spaced repetition. Store ease, interval, repetitions, due date per card. Grading buttons: again, hard, good, easy. Due queue per deck, capped at a configurable daily limit.
5. Quiz mode: pull 10 due or random mcq cards, score at the end, log the attempt.
6. Stats page: cards due today, reviews per day for the last 30 days as a simple bar chart, retention percentage.
7. Export a deck to Anki-compatible CSV and to JSON. Import the same JSON back.

Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, sharing, payments, audio or video transcription, OCR, image occlusion, mobile app, any hosted deployment.

Requirements: seed the database with one demo deck of 8 cards so study mode is testable without an API key. Keyboard shortcuts in study mode (space to reveal, 1-4 to grade). One `npm run dev` starts API and UI together. README with setup, .env.example, and one paragraph on where the SM-2 constants live so I can tune them.
